## One tree over the copies, or one over all of them

64x32, 32 triangles a copy. Flattened means every vertex of every copy transformed on
the host and given one tree; two-level keeps one tree over one copy and walks a
second tree over the placements.

| Copies | Flat triangles | Flat work | Flat KB | Two-level triangles | Work | KB | Memory | Work |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 4 | 128 | 3,108,698 | 7.2 | 32 | 3,516,844 | 2.3 | **3.1x** | 0.88x |
| 16 | 512 | 5,185,318 | 28.5 | 32 | 6,769,990 | 3.9 | **7.2x** | 0.77x |
| 64 | 2048 | 11,036,896 | 114.7 | 32 | 17,221,439 | 10.5 | **10.9x** | 0.64x |
| 256 | 8192 | 35,314,678 | 457.6 | 32 | 60,319,951 | 36.8 | **12.5x** | 0.59x |

Memory is what the second level buys and the ratio grows with the copies: one
tree over the geometry however many there are. Work goes the other way, and by
a widening margin — an instance visited costs sixteen scalar loads to fetch its
matrix, the wide global matrix load the naming scheme reserves not being built.
